Source to reuse: scripts/ringer/environment_narration/drain_details_capture.py (`_run_engine`, how it builds a real engine state, stubs `CloudflareTurnProvider._request`, skips item_facts requests and records narrator requests), drain_details_prose_probe.py (`run_rows`: the billed loop, stop reasons, label freeze, blind sheets, `_usd_ceiling`), drain_condition_judge_probe.py (`variant_b_payload`, `_row`, `_score`, `_verdict`, `run_cases`, `JevClient`, `UNUSABLE_STOP_AFTER`), enforce_t9h_drain_details.sh and enforce_t9h_drain_condition_judge.sh (local Worker start, port guard, refuse-if-rows-exist, cleanup trap). Import from those scripts with importlib (as drain_details_capture.py does) instead of copying, where practical. The Variant B question wording must be the imported one, byte-identical.

CONTEXT: the story package now declares a story sub-kind `opening` (data/stories/continuity-initiative/world.yaml `kinds:`), set on back_door, house_gate, facility_gate, service_gate and storm_drain. The experiment asks whether the existing Variant B judge separates forbidden from clean narrations about the four openings other than the drain.

BUILD `opening_condition_v2.py` with these modes (argparse, one mode per call):
1. `--capture --out FILE` (free, offline). Load the package; read the class as every item whose declared kind is (or descends from) `opening`, using WorldSchema.kind_is on world_source_schema_data(package.world); exclude `storm_drain` (EXCLUDED = {"storm_drain"}). A table PROMPTS maps thing id -> (scene_id, protagonist place id, command): back_door ("1A", "kitchen", "Inspect the back door."), house_gate ("1A", "outside_house", "Inspect the house gate."), service_gate ("1B", "los_angeles_park", "Inspect the service gate."), facility_gate ("2A", "facility_perimeter", "Inspect the facility gate."). Refuse (exit non-zero, clear message) if the class minus EXCLUDED differs from the table keys, so the class is read from the package and the table only supplies the turn. For each thing: build the real engine state for that scene with the protagonist placed in that place (enter the scene the way the existing probes do, then place the protagonist through the world model; find how the scene-1B probe and tests such as tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py `_state_at` do it), run `engine.opening()` then `engine.turn(command)` with `CloudflareTurnProvider._request` stubbed exactly as `_run_engine` does, and record the FIRST narrator request of the turn (system starts with "You are the narrator") as the full payload dict the engine passed to `_request`, minus keys that start with "__" (keep max_tokens, response_format or anything else it sends, so the billed replay is verbatim). Per thing write {thing_id, name (declared name), scene_id, place_id, command, status: "captured" | "not reproducible offline", error, request}. Per-thing failures are recorded, not raised. Write {schema, stage: "t9h-opening-v2", package_world_sha256, things: [...]}.
2. `--run --capture FILE --samples N --max-calls M --max-usd X --confirm --out FILE` (billed; you never run it). Plan = captured things x samples (10 frozen; refuse other values). Refuse when planned > max-calls, when the USD ceiling (same token estimate approach as drain_details_prose_probe) exceeds max-usd, without --confirm, when out exists, when fewer than 3 things are captured, and when CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL or CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN is unset; all refusals happen before writing anything. Send each captured request verbatim through `CloudflareTurnProvider(...)._request` like `run_rows`. Rows: {call_index, thing_id, command, sample, response_text, narration}, where narration is the joined `segments[].text` when response_text parses as the narrator JSON, else the raw text. Record stop_reason (None when complete) and write after every call.
3. `--blind-sheet --rows FILE --out DIR`: sheet.md (narration only, fixed-seed shuffle, opaque ids sample-001.., no thing id, command, call index or file path in the sheet), blind_key.json (opaque id -> call_index), labels_template.json with null values for exactly these names: opens_or_enters, invents_open_state, asserts_definite_contents, speculative_only, asserts_closed_or_locked, wrong_place.
4. `--freeze-labels --labels FILE`: writes `<labels stem>.freeze.json` beside it with the SHA-256 of the finished file; refuses null labels, refuses an existing freeze with a different hash.
5. `--build-cases --rows FILE --labels FILE --key FILE --out DIR`: requires a matching freeze. forbidden = opens_or_enters or invents_open_state or asserts_definite_contents. Writes DIR/cases.jsonl with exactly the judge probe's CASE_FIELDS {id, set: "opening", thing (declared name), command, narration, declared, forbidden, source_ref (thing_id/sample-N)} and DIR/lock.json {cases_sha256, case_count}. declared = "the <declared name> has no open or closed value, no declared contents, and is fixed in place." and is built only for things of kind opening (refuse any other thing).
6. `--judge --cases DIR --samples 5 --max-calls K --max-usd Y --min-interval-s S --confirm --out FILE` (billed; you never run it): requires the lock to match; Variant B ONLY (5 samples x cases); refuse when planned > max-calls, the ceiling exceeds max-usd, without --confirm, when out exists or credentials are unset. Reuse the judge probe's row format, scoring, pacing and unusable-stop behaviour (you may call its run_cases with a planned list restricted to B, or write a thin loop that reuses its helpers). Also support `--dry-run` printing the planned count and ceiling.
7. `--report --cases DIR --rows FILE --out FILE`: per-case median of the case's scores; accepted above .65, rejected below .35, else uncertain (counts against both conditions). Verdict per the preregistration: INCONCLUSIVE if the rows are partial (stop_reason not None or fewer rows than planned) or fewer than 10 forbidden or fewer than 10 clean cases; PASS if forbidden rejected >= 90% and clean accepted >= 90%; else FAIL. Report counts per condition and per thing, the per-case medians, and the gate line. Print the verdict.

`enforce_t9h_opening_v2.sh generate|judge`: modeled on the two enforce scripts. generate: OUT=bench/results/environment-narration/t9h-opening-v2, runs --capture to $OUT/capture.json if it is absent, starts `node scripts/ringer/environment_narration/local_worker.mjs --port 8811 --max-usd 0.06`, waits for /__spent, exports CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL, runs `--run --confirm --samples 10 --max-calls 40 --max-usd 0.06 --out $OUT/generate/rows.json`. judge: port 8812, worker --max-usd 0.02, runs `--judge --confirm --samples 5 --max-calls 200 --max-usd 0.02 --min-interval-s 0.5 --cases $OUT/cases --out $OUT/judge/rows.json`, then `--report` to $OUT/report.md. Both refuse if the port is in use or the rows exist. Keep the literal flag strings shown (the check greps for them).

TESTS (tests/test_opening_condition_v2.py, hermetic): capture on the real package returns the four things with the command in each narrator prompt and excludes storm_drain; capture refuses when the class and table differ (synthetic); run refuses each guard case before writing; run with a stub provider writes rows and joins segments; blind sheet leaks nothing (forbidden words list) and shuffles deterministically; freeze refuses nulls and a changed hash; build-cases requires the freeze, computes forbidden, uses the exact declared sentence and the probe's CASE_FIELDS; judge plans only Variant B and the payload question equals the probe's variant_b_payload output; report gives PASS, FAIL and each INCONCLUSIVE branch on synthetic rows.

HOW TO VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH: run `bash /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/check_t9h_opening_v2.sh`. Finish with a short summary: the exact CLI per mode, which things captured, and anything that could not be reproduced offline (with the error).
